name: Lombard (classical Milanese orthography)

ancestors.notes: Same language, same phonology; only the accented-vowel orthographic convention differs (see notes).

notes: Lombard written in the classical Milanese orthography (the Circolo Filologico Milanese's revision of Porta-era usage) rather than the Ticinese orthography that `lmo` targets. The two conventions genuinely diverge on the circumflex series and cannot both be served by one spec: the classical-Milanese source ('Ortografia milanese classica', 'Accenti' section, citing Porta, Poesie, ed. Isella, Mondadori 1982) states the circumflex marks a 'very closed timbre and long duration', and separately states plain 'o' is already pronounced as Italian 'u' in Milanese — so a circumflex applied to that already-[u] vowel gives [oː] by the source's stated closed+long rule read literally (the timbre component targets [o], distinct from the plain-o value [u]; the length component is the source's explicit claim). `lmo` instead maps ô to plain /u/ with no length, a choice measured against the WikiPron gold's two attested circumflex-o words ('rasô', 'resô'), both realized as /u/ with no length — a gold-fit reading, not the source's own rule. This entry ships the source's rule literally instead of the gold-fit reading: ô=/oː/, â=/aː/ (length only, since Lombard does not distinguish open/closed timbre on 'a'). Everything else — grave/acute accented vowels, ü/ö front rounded vowels, consonants, degemination, and the whole galloitalic-derived allophone table — is identical phonology to `lmo` and is inherited via `graphemes_base`/`allophones_base` rather than duplicated, per orthography2ipa's one-concept-one-place rule for orthography variants of the same language (compare `cdo-Latn-buc`, `zh-Hani`, and the `-x-` regional-orthography entries). No official body publishes the classical Milanese orthography — unlike Ticinese's CDE Canton Ticino, it is an editorial tradition maintained by the Circolo Filologico Milanese and by individual editors (e.g. Isella's 1982 edition of Porta); accordingly no `orthography_standard` is declared here. This entry is not scored against the existing `lmo`/wikipron benchmark row: that gold is overwhelmingly Ticinese-spelled (95 of 406 unique words use the Ticinese grave/acute series against 7 circumflex + 6 umlaut words in the classical-Milanese minority), so repointing or splitting that row would not improve its measurement of either convention. This entry exists to model the classical-Milanese circumflex rule correctly on its own terms, for a gold that is actually written in that convention, not to win points against a row that is not.

sources.author: Porta, Carlo (ed. Isella, Dante)
sources.title: Poesie
sources.notes: The classical Milanese literary orthography this entry targets, as codified in Isella's critical edition of Porta's verse and summarized by the Circolo Filologico Milanese's 'Accenti' rule (circumflex = closed timbre + length; plain 'o' already pronounced [u]). Edition not directly consulted; the rule is reported via its Wikipedia summary (see ortografia_milanese_classica_wp), not read from the edition itself.
